rows.name: Beguiling Hex {@recharge 5}
entries: The horror expels a wave of mind-altering magic. Each creature within 30 feet of the horror must make a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw, taking 33 ({@damage 6d10}) psychic damage and being {@condition incapacitated} until the end of the creature's next turn on a failed save, or taking half as much damage on a successful one.

rows.name: Bile Hex {@recharge 5}
entries: The horror expels acidic bile in a 60-foot line that is 5 feet wide. Each creature in that line must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or be covered in bile. A creature covered in bile takes 31 ({@damage 7d8}) acid damage at the start of each of its turns until it or another creature uses its action to scrape or wash off the bile that covers it.

rows.name: Petrifying Hex {@recharge 5}
entries: The horror expels petrifying gas in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in that area must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or take 14 ({@damage 4d6}) necrotic damage and be {@condition restrained} as it begins to turn to stone. A {@condition restrained} creature must repeat the saving throw at the end of its next turn. On a success, the effect ends on the target. On a failure, the target is {@condition petrified} until freed by the {@spell greater restoration} spell or other magic.

rows.name: Reality-Stealing Hex {@recharge 5}
entries: The horror expels a wave of perception-distorting energy. Each creature within 30 feet of the horror must make a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 22 ({@damage 5d8}) psychic damage and is {@condition deafened} until the end of its next turn. If the saving throw fails by 5 or more, the target is also {@condition blinded} until the end of its next turn.

en.caption: Gothic Horror Torments
rows: The Darklord's soul is so consumed by shadows that it extinguishes all light that shines on them.
The Darklord inherited unlimited wealth, but finery she wears turns to rags and food tastes like ash.
The Darklord is incomparably beautiful, but locals perceive him as a terrible beast.
Tattoos detailing the Darklord's sins cover their body.
Every night, the Darklord is the focus of a lavish ball, but during the day he turns into a lead statue.
A choir of spirits follows the Darklord, endlessly singing her sins.
The Darklord endlessly cries tears of blood, ink, poison, or molten iron.
The Darklord knows how he's going to die and sees evidence of impending doom everywhere.

en.caption: Grand Masquerade Complications
rows: An angry guest with a costume identical to a character's accuses them of stealing the idea.
A flirtatious guest decides these interesting characters deserve to be introduced to the city's elite.
The character with the highest passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) score notices a nimble-fingered guest slipping a necklace off their dance partner.
An intoxicated guest loudly confesses truths that other guests pretend not to hear.
A scream from a different part of the estate pierces the air. Everyone hushes for a moment, then immediately carries on as if nothing had happened.
Duchess Saidra enters the room, and sycophants immediately surround her.
en.name: Grand Masquerade Complications

en.caption: Dark Fantasy Plots
rows: Track down a beholder-shaped flesh golem and learn why it's targeting specific individuals.
Seal a portal to a demonic realm that opens within the mouth of an innocent acolyte.
Cure a virus turning people into shadows.
Mount a defense against the swarm of giant spiders that's declared war on bipeds.
Prevent a mighty spell that a coven of witches is casting using a volcanic caldera as a cauldron.
Keep a nation from tearing itself apart when it's revealed the beloved ruler is a lich.
Banish a spirit haunting the moon.
Uncover the identity of an otherworldly coward who's hiding among mortals, avoiding the destructive search of the immortals they fled.
en.name: Dark Fantasy Plots

en.caption: Body Horror Settings
rows: A country of red muscle, with bleeding eyes embedded in the hair-strangled trees
A world of monuments and houses, all made of flesh
A domain ordinary save for the abundance of black hair, the strands always moving even when there is no breeze
A neighborhood of derelict houses, each one composed of numerous mimics
An ocean of undead leviathans, still moving despite the entrails bubbling from their burst torsos
A forest of black pines draped in bodies
A slaughterhouse larger than it appears on the outside, full of victims mutely awaiting slaughter
A system of subterranean tunnels, their walls spackled with fossils or mummified organs

en.caption: Bluetspur Adventures
rows: Characters awake within the shattered remains of a fluid-filled tube deep in Citadel Subterrene. They have no idea how they arrived there.
A cavern the characters were exploring seamlessly abuts with Bluetspur, trapping them in caves overrun with {@creature Vampiric Mind Flayer|VRGR|vampiric mind flayers} (see {@area chapter 5|57c|x}).
A strange message leads characters to a silvery vessel full of alien mysteries wrecked on Bluetspur's surface. The only surviving creature in the wreck is a cunning {@creature displacer beast}.

The characters find a strange but adorable creature trapped within an abandoned alien installation. The being is a lovable companion, until it reveals itself to be a {@filter star spawn emissary|bestiary|source=RHW|group=Star Spawn Emissary}.
An acquaintance of the characters complains of reoccurring nightmares. The complaints stop when the dreamer is taken over by an {@creature intellect devourer}.

An inventor requests the characters' insight into a pill-sized device she extracted from her own body. As the characters examine it, the device projects a map into their minds and emits a telepathic call for help. The map leads to a {@creature mind flayer} who wants to put the God-Brain out of its misery.
A farmer hires the characters to protect his family, whom he believes—without evidence—are being abducted and returned every night.

The High Master mind flayer of Mount Grysl seeks to claim all the God-Brain knows. To do this, it creates a copy of the Apparatus (see "{@area Mordent|0fa|x}" later in this chapter). All it needs is a relic called the Rod of Rastinon, which it wants the characters to retrieve for it.
en.name: Bluetspur Adventures
